question.text: Value at Risk (VaR) of 95% one-month VaR = Rs. 1 crore means:

answer.text: The fund WILL lose Rs. 1 crore over next month
There is 95% probability the loss over next month will NOT exceed Rs. 1 crore
The fund gains Rs. 1 crore with 95% confidence

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explains that a 95 percent one-month VaR of Rs. 1 crore means there is a 95 percent probability that over the next month the fund will not lose more than Rs. 1 crore. VaR is the maximum expected loss over a defined timeframe at a stated confidence level. The Trap: VaR is a probabilistic loss estimate, not a guaranteed loss or gain, and it is not the hurdle rate used in incentive-fee computations. Note: Per workbook pages 225-226.
